_doc: Content for /programme-room (tools/build-programme-room.py). Every statement is taken from the Evidence library cards, the Study progress records (study.html) or approved site wording. Items flagged in records/SOURCE-REGISTER.md as lacking source evidence (Phase 2B sponsor role; Phase 2B participant numbers, doses and duration) are deliberately not repeated. Two separate label sets: 'work' (the status of programme activity, per stage) and 'types' (what kind of source supports a statement, per source). Approval status is never inferred from missing public documentation. Source dates ('Source date', 'Record date') and website review dates ('Website page reviewed') are kept apart; an unknown date says 'Not available'.

stages.title: Why people at clinical high risk are a research priority
stages.question: What is known about people who meet criteria for clinical high risk of psychosis (CHR-P), and what care is recommended today?
known: CHR-P is not a diagnosis of psychosis or schizophrenia, and most people in this group do not develop psychosis.
An updated meta-analysis estimated that about one in four people identified as CHR-P (pooled estimate, 25%) developed psychosis within three years.
In England, psychological therapy is the recommended first step. NICE advises against antipsychotics to prevent psychosis in this group.
No preventive intervention has been shown to work better than the others.
stages.further: Larger, well-designed trials in this group. For each intervention studied so far, the trials are few and small.

stages.title: An oral softgel designed for a poorly water-soluble medicine
stages.question: Is a fixed-strength micellar softgel a suitable way to give cannabidiol by mouth?
known: Cannabidiol dissolves poorly in water. Taken by mouth while fasting, only about 6% of a dose is estimated to reach the bloodstream, and food changes absorption markedly (research on other CBD products).
NWPT-SM32300 is a 300 mg softgel whose contents are designed to disperse into very small droplets in the gut.
The final formulation and GMP clinical supply were completed before Phase 1 dosing in 2025 (company records).
stages.further: Whether this formulation gives more consistent absorption than other CBD products. Phase 1 measured absorption; its results have not been published. How much reaches the brain has not been measured.

stages.question: How does the body absorb and handle NWPT-SM32300 after single doses, and how well is it tolerated in the short term, compared with a licensed cannabidiol oral solution?
known: 14 healthy adult volunteers; randomised, open-label, three-period crossover.
Sponsor of the Phase 1 study: NWPharmaTech Ltd (as registered).
It was not a study of whether NWPT-SM32300 works.
Study activity ended on 10 December 2025. Results have not yet been published.
stages.further: The Phase 1 results, once published, would show how NWPT-SM32300 was absorbed and tolerated after single doses. Effectiveness in people at clinical high risk would need a separate study, such as the planned Phase 2B.

stages.title: The planned Phase 2B study in people at clinical high risk
stages.question: What would the planned Phase 2B study investigate?
known: Status: planned. Not recruiting. The protocol is being finalised.
The Phase 2B study can start only after regulatory and research ethics approval.
Oversight arrangements for the Phase 2B study have not yet been published.
A larger UK trial of cannabidiol in this group (CANTOP-RCT) did not start owing to challenges in securing supply of the study drug, which is one reason this question remains open.
A small 21-day study of another CBD product in this group was published in 2024. Its findings are early, have not been confirmed in a larger trial, and do not apply directly to NWPT-SM32300.
stages.further: If it goes ahead: whether NWPT-SM32300 shows a dose response, changes symptoms, and is safe and tolerable in people at clinical high risk of psychosis.

open_questions: Does NWPT-SM32300 reduce symptoms in people at clinical high risk?
Not established. It would take the results of a pre-specified clinical study such as the planned Phase 2B.
Is there a dose response, and which dose would be best?
Not established. Dose response is one of the planned study’s aims.
Is it safe and well tolerated in this population?
Not established. Phase 1 involved healthy volunteers and single doses only.
Does the formulation give more consistent absorption than other CBD products?
Not published. Phase 1 measured absorption; its results are awaited.
Can transition to psychosis be delayed or prevented?
A longer-term question needing a separately powered trial with long follow-up.
